source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Small to very large evergreen tree
morphology_documented.leaves: Leaf shape variable; genus white-oak key compares generally cuneate blade bases with broader, rounded-based Q. fusiformis
morphology_documented.fruit: Key comparison: usually ovoid blunt mature acorns 15–20(–25) mm long, commonly half or less emergent from cup
morphology_documented.habitat: Flora considers true wild Q. virginiana naturally southeast of its north-central Texas coverage

source_scope_note: Historical species treatments and explicitly identified genus/key characteristics only; missing morphology not inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Historical flora documents extensive hybridization/introgression with Q. fusiformis and warns that central Texas live-oak identifications may be ambiguous
Cultivated occurrence is not county-level BONAP nativity evidence
preservation: Additive record only, original species and photo/credits/gallery unchanged
